East Fishkill Town Court is a justice city courthouse in the County of Duchess, New York. It is located within the 9th and 2nd Judicial District Departments. The court has jurisdiction over small claims and eviction, traffic and vehicle matters. This court handles mostly speeding tickets given on I-84 and Taconic. The court session is held on every Tuesday and Wednesday.

Jurisdiction of the East Fishkill Town Court

The East Fishkill Town Court has limited jurisdiction, which means that it can only hear certain types of cases. Its jurisdiction includes:

  • Traffic Violations: The court can hear cases involving traffic violations that occur within the town of East Fishkill, such as speeding tickets, red light violations, and parking tickets.
  • Misdemeanors: The court can hear cases involving misdemeanors that occur within the town of East Fishkill, such as petty theft, disorderly conduct, and drug possession.
  • Small Claims: The court can hear civil cases involving claims for money damages up to $3,000.

Cases Handled by the East Fishkill Town Court

The East Fishkill Town Court handles a variety of cases, including:

  • Traffic Violations: As mentioned earlier, the court hears cases involving traffic violations that occur within the town of East Fishkill. These cases can result in fines, points on your driver's license, and even license suspension.
  • Misdemeanors: The court also hears cases involving misdemeanors that occur within the town of East Fishkill. If you are convicted of a misdemeanor, you may face fines, probation, or even jail time.
  • Small Claims: The court can hear civil cases involving claims for money damages up to $3,000. These cases can involve disputes over rent, contracts, and personal injuries.

Location and Contact Information of the East Fishkill Town Court

The East Fishkill Town Court is located at:

2468 Route 52 Hopewell Junction, NY 12533

You can contact the court by phone at (845) 226-4229 or by fax at (845) 226-7937. The court is open from Monday to Friday, from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

East Fishkill Town Court Procedures

If you are facing legal issues in the East Fishkill Town Court, it is important to understand the court's procedures. The following are some of the key procedures you should be aware of:

  • Arraignments: An arraignment is the first court appearance you will have if you are charged with a crime. At the arraignment, the judge will inform you of the charges against you and ask how you plead. If you plead not guilty, the court will schedule a trial date.
  • Plea Bargains: Before a trial, you may be offered a plea bargain. A plea bargain is an agreement between you and the prosecution where you plead guilty to a lesser charge in exchange for a reduced sentence.
  • Trials: If you plead not guilty or reject a plea bargain, your case will go to trial. Trials can be either bench trials (where the judge decides the verdict) or jury trials (where a group of citizens decides the verdict).

Court Resources for Defendants

If you are facing legal issues in the East Fishkill Town Court, you may be able to take advantage of several resources that can help you navigate the legal system. These resources include:

  • Legal Assistance: If you cannot afford an attorney, you may be able to get free legal assistance through Legal Services of the Hudson Valley.
  • Court-Appointed Attorneys: If you cannot afford an attorney, the court may appoint one for you. However, court-appointed attorneys are only available for criminal cases.
  • Online Resources: The New York State Unified Court System website provides a wealth of information on court procedures and legal resources.

How to file a small claims case?

East Fishkill Town Court small claims cases can be filled by filling out the small claims application form available at the clerk's office. You should tell the person's name and address, the reason for the claims, and the amount you claim in the application form. The maximum limit for a claim is $3000. The filing fee is $10 for claims less than $1000 and $15 for claims up to $3000. The person against which cases occur must be the resident of this town, and if the case is related to the property, then that property must also be in this town.

How to find CAse Information?

East Fishkill Town Court case search information and records are available at the court office in files, on the computer, and online. They can be found online by using the following ways:

  • Searching by name
  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by address
  • Searching by phone
  • Searching by email

Some information about cases is not available online because they are confidential by law, like marriage, birth records etc. These types of information are only available at the court office. You had to submit a form for this information by visiting the court, and then the court would respond whether to provide the record information or not. Mostly confidential information is only given to the person involved in the case or to the police or investigation agency. The record search request is free of cost.

The traffic court handles which types of cases?

The town of East Fishkill Traffic Court handles cases of traffic and vehicle violations. The violation includes speeding, accidents, using cell phones while driving, failing to follow a traffic signal or traffic control device, driving while intoxicated, with a suspended or no license, leaving the scene of the accident, and driving recklessly. A motorist cannot respond to the ticket. You can send a guilty or not guilty plea to the court before the date written on the ticket you received. The court will respond whether to appear in the court for the case or only fines will be paid. If you do not pay the fine or on time, then your driving license and driving privilege will be suspended. You cannot request your license renewal until the court approves. The Police Department of the Town gives the speeding ticket. Hire a professional traffic Ticket attorney for traffic and speeding cases because they can defend you against the traffic charges in court.

How many fines and points are received for traffic violence?

East Fishkill Town Court traffic violence fines depend upon a person's violation. For example, $45 to $600 penalties for a first-time speeding offense, up to $1575 for one or more speeding tickets within eighteen months, $100 – $300 fine for a traffic infraction, $25-$200 for driving an unregistered vehicle or trailer, $200 – $1225 for a misdemeanor conviction and $50- $55 for surcharges. Three points will be deducted if the speed is 01 to 10 mph over the limit, 6 for speed over 21 to 30 and 11 if the speed is over 40 mph. An increase in points will result in the suspension of the license.

How to make payments?

East Fishkill Town Court pay ticket, and other fines can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay for traffic tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the counter. 2.99% convince and other charges will be applied if you pay with a credit card.

Online

A person can pay online by using the online payment website https://www.ncourt.com/. Enter your traffic ticket or other fine information and pay the fine. Processing fees will be applied in this online method.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address. The address is 330 NY-376, Hopewell Junction, NY 12533, United States. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks are accepted.

How to get a marriage license?

East Fishkill Town Court's marriage license is obtained from the clerk's office and given by the Dutchess County health department. The appointment is mandatory for getting the marriage license. The fee for a marriage license is $40 and for certificates is $10 per copy. The couple's age must be 18+. If someone is under 18, written consent from parents, guardians, and the judge is mandatory. To get the certification, the couple had to submit a marriage form with an original sealed birth certificate issued by the state, photo ids like a driver's license, Passport, or anything that could prove their identity. The application form is available at the clerk's office. If this is anyone's second marriage, a divorce paper or spouse death certificate must be required at the time of registration. All the documents must be in English. If anyone wants the copies, fill out the certificated copy of the marriage license request, and submit it to the court.

What is the role of the clerk?

East Fishkill Town Court clerk's role is to maintain each case file and receive and handle payment and fines. The clerk's office is the center of town business and the primary source of information regarding the town. They are responsible for the maintenance of all Official Town Records and the issuance of various licenses. They are an agent of licensing and custodians of the town records. They provide marriage licenses, birth and death certificates, permits, etc.

Conclusion

The East Fishkill Town Court is an important part of the legal system in Dutchess County, New York. Whether you are facing a traffic ticket or a criminal charge, it is important to understand the court's jurisdiction and procedures. By taking advantage of the court's resources for defendants, you can increase your chances of a successful outcome.

FAQ:

How can I contact the town clerk?

Visit the clerk's office during working hours or call them.

Phone: 845-221-9191

What is the timing for a court session?

The timing for the court session is:

  • Tuesday: 9:00 am
  • Wednesday: 4:00 pm

How can I request the deposition certificate?

Download the request for certification of disposition application form from the website, fill in all the information and send it to court. $5 is the fee for getting the certificate.

What are the types of acceptable identification for getting the certificate and license?

Acceptable identification for getting the certificate and license are:

  • Driving or Non-Driving License
  • Passport
  • Military ID
  • Employers Photo ID

What are the fees for filling out a form or petition?

$20 is the fee for the filling of a form or petition.
